title: Managed DISABLED Claude row: its not-run updateDetail must not tell the user to enable it (ruling 28 follow-up)
description: Found by the adversarial review of LCLI-604 (opum-ai/lore-cli#305), finding S1. When the deciding Claude row has scope managed and state disabled, lore agents --target claude --force reports update not-run with the ordinary disabled detail: "lore agents never enables a disabled plugin; enable it with the remedy, then update". Next to the agreed managed remedy ("...which only an administrator can change"), that tells the user to do something only an administrator can do, and promises an update that ruling 28 says never happens. A bare lore agents --force on the same row also says "lore agents --target claude --force updates this one", which is false. Only the list runs in both cases, so the wording is wrong but no wrong action is taken. Proposed fix: use the agreed managed updateDetail ("the deciding row is managed by your Claude Code administrator, so it is never updated") for installed AND disabled managed rows. That widens the scope of a ruling-(d) string, so it needs quest-cli to agree for parity (proposed to quest-cli 2026-09-26, no answer when this was filed); implement only once it is agreed, or once opum-agent rules.

acceptanceCriteria.text: quest-cli has agreed (or opum-agent has ruled) which updateDetail a managed disabled row carries, recorded here with the agreement

A managed disabled row under --target claude --force and under a bare --force carries that detail, and no detail on a managed row mentions enabling or a runnable update, proven through a stub port that logs every call
bun test and bun run lore check exit 0
